kintampo-complex.name: Kintampo Complex
kintampo-complex.summary: A West African prehistoric culture active roughly 2500 to 1400 BCE, established by Saharan agropastoralists and marking a shift from pastoralism to settled life, known for early figurative art, stone tools and structures.

nok-culture.name: Nok culture
nok-culture.summary: An ancient population in what is now Nigeria, named for the village where its terracotta sculptures were first found in 1928, existing from roughly 1500 BCE to 1 CE.

dhar-tichitt.name: Dhar Tichitt
dhar-tichitt.summary: A line of sandstone cliffs in southwestern Mauritania with Neolithic sites inhabited by pastoralists and farmers between about 2000 and 300 BCE, among the oldest known settlements in West Africa.

tichitt-tradition.name: Tichitt tradition
tichitt-tradition.summary: A proto-Mande culture (2200–200 BCE) in what is now Mauritania, known for hierarchical settlements, farming and metallurgy at sites like Dhar Tichitt.

elam.name: Elam
elam.summary: An ancient civilization centered in western and southwestern Iran, one of the leading political forces of the ancient Near East, with written records from around 3000 BCE.

incense-trade-route.name: Incense trade route
incense-trade-route.summary: Ancient network of land and sea trade routes linking the Mediterranean with sources of incense, spices, and luxury goods, flourishing from about the 3rd century BC to the 2nd century AD.

hanno-the-navigator.name: Hanno the Navigator
hanno-the-navigator.summary: A Carthaginian explorer of the 5th century BC known for a naval expedition along West Africa's coast, described in an account (periplus) that may show him reaching as far as modern Gabon.

nsibidi.name: Nsibidi
nsibidi.summary: A system of symbols, or proto-writing, developed by the Ejagham people of the Cross River region of Nigeria and Cameroon, used in wall designs, tattoos, and secret-society rituals.

ikom-monoliths.name: Ikom monoliths
ikom-monoliths.summary: A series of volcanic-stone monoliths near Ikom, Nigeria, likely carved by the Ejagham people around 200 CE and also known as Akwaanshi or Atal.

ikom.name: Ikom
ikom.summary: A farming town and local government area in Cross River State, Nigeria, known for the ancient inscribed Afi monoliths and for producing cocoa, bananas and plantains.

a-r-mountains.name: Aïr Mountains
a-r-mountains.summary: A triangular mountain massif in the Sahara of northern Niger, rising over 1,800 m, whose Sahel-like climate has long supported farming, herding and notable archaeological sites.

niger-congo-languages.name: Niger–Congo languages
niger-congo-languages.summary: A proposed family of African languages spoken across most of sub-Saharan Africa, including Yoruba, Igbo, Swahili and Zulu, and possibly the world's largest by number of languages.

lejja.name: Lejja
lejja.summary: A community of 33 villages in southeastern Nigeria with iron-smelting evidence dating to 2000 BC, among the earliest known ironworking sites in sub-Saharan Africa.

abidemi-babatunde-babalola.name: Babalola
abidemi-babatunde-babalola.summary: Nigerian archaeologist and British Museum research fellow, lead archaeologist for the Museum of West African Art, who won the Dan David Prize from Tel Aviv University in 2025.

nsukka.name: Nsukka
nsukka.summary: A city and local government area in Enugu State, Nigeria, home to the University of Nigeria.

igboland.name: Igboland
igboland.summary: The cultural and linguistic homeland of the Igbo people in southern Nigeria, an informal region with no official government, spanning several states and diverse local traditions.

aoukar.name: Aoukar (Hodh Depression)
aoukar.summary: A dry basin of sand dunes and salt pans in southeastern Mauritania, also known as Hodh or El Hodh.

mand-peoples.name: Mandé peoples
mand-peoples.summary: A broader grouping of West African peoples, including the Mandinka, who speak related Mande languages and share a common caste system, predominantly Muslim today.

soninke-people.name: Soninke
soninke-people.summary: A West African Mande-speaking ethnic group who founded the ancient empire of Ghana (Wagadou), around 200 to 1240 CE, later spreading widely as traders.

kaduna-state.name: Kaduna State
kaduna-state.summary: State in northwest Nigeria home to the Nok civilization (c. 1500 BC to 500 AD) and later part of the Sokoto Caliphate; became capital of the British Northern Nigeria Protectorate.

if.name: Ile-Ife
if.summary: An ancient Yoruba city in southwestern Nigeria founded between 1000 and 500 BC, famed by 900 AD for sophisticated bronze, stone and terracotta art.
